editor_note: Entry 15 keeps the meaning of the English. Exclusive access, "no other jobs can run, including calibration jobs", variational algorithms, parallelism in the stack and the cost function on the user's local machine are all there, and the terms (job, jobs de calibration, charge de travail multi-jobs) match the rest of the file, e.g. entry 11. The one thing a native editor would fix is "éviter les délais causés par la mise en file de chaque job séparément". In French "délai" means an allotted time span, not a hold-up, so this should read "retards" (or "temps d'attente"). "mise en file" is also clipped; it should be "mise en file d'attente". A learner would not be misled.

examples.source: Using sessions helps avoid delays caused by queuing each job separately
examples.translation: L'utilisation des sessions aide à éviter les délais causés par la mise en file de chaque job séparément
examples.suggested: Les sessions permettent d'éviter les retards dus à la mise en file d'attente de chaque job séparément
examples.why: "Délai" means an allotted time span, so using it for "delay" is a calque. "Retards" or "temps d'attente" is the idiomatic word, and "mise en file" is clipped where "mise en file d'attente" is expected. Meaning is intact.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through. The run() capacity checks [34], the job status list [39]-[49], the note that the runtime jobs list can be empty [57] and the log filters [60] all match the English, and the "tu" register holds. The problems are small. The same IBM Cloud link names are translated in [25] ("Clés API IBM Cloud", "Gestion des clés API utilisateur", "rubrique") but left in English in [27] ("IBM Cloud API keys", "Managing user API keys", "sujet"). [4] uses the calque "ayant contribué une fonction au catalogue", since transitive "contribuer" is an anglicism.

examples.source: on the [IBM Cloud API keys] page ... Learn more in the [Managing user API keys] topic.
examples.translation: sur la page [IBM Cloud API keys] ... consulte le sujet [Managing user API keys]
examples.suggested: sur la page [Clés API IBM Cloud] ... consulte la rubrique [Gestion des clés API utilisateur]
examples.why: Entry [25] translates these same link names and uses 'rubrique', so [27] is inconsistent with it.

examples.source: one of the partners who have contributed a function to the catalog
examples.translation: l'un des partenaires ayant contribué une fonction au catalogue
examples.suggested: l'un des partenaires ayant fourni une fonction au catalogue
examples.why: Transitive 'contribuer quelque chose' is an anglicism. 'Fournir' or 'contribuer au catalogue avec une fonction' reads as native French.

examples.source: The function is optimizing for the selected QPU.
examples.translation: La fonction optimise pour la QPU sélectionnée.
examples.suggested: La fonction optimise le calcul pour la QPU sélectionnée.
examples.why: 'Optimiser' with no object is a stiff calque in French. Adding an object reads more naturally.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing here would mislead a learner. The IDP/SSO/SAML terms and the "(peut engendrer des coûts)" caveat are kept, and "tu" is used consistently. Two small polish points: [3] "Tu peux intégrer ton fournisseur d'identité externe" is a slight calque of "integrate with". A native editor would write "intégrer IBM Cloud à ton fournisseur…" or "t'intégrer à". In the Recommendations list [9], the infinitive "Voir le …" breaks the "Consulte …" imperative used in the lines around it.

examples.source: You can integrate with your external identity provider (IDP)
examples.translation: Tu peux intégrer ton fournisseur d'identité externe (IDP)
examples.suggested: Tu peux intégrer ton compte à ton fournisseur d'identité externe (IDP)
examples.why: 'intégrer X' reads as absorbing the IDP itself, not integrating with it; this is a light calque.

examples.source: See [IBM Cloud SAML Federation Guide] for more information.
examples.translation: Voir le [Guide de fédération SAML IBM Cloud] pour plus d'informations.
examples.suggested: Consulte le [Guide de fédération SAML IBM Cloud] pour plus d'informations.
examples.why: The infinitive 'Voir' is inconsistent with the 'Consulte' imperative in the neighbouring bullets and the tu register.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout, with no misleading drift. The twirling precedence rule, the PEA/PEC caveat and the Clifford-simulation limits are all rendered faithfully. The main defect is a grammar error: the tu imperative 'Mets à jour' is written 'Met à jour' four times in the migration tables ([20], [22]). The English table header 'Change | Migration action' was also left untranslated. 'Unique layers' / 'unique-layer helper' became 'couches uniques' / 'assistant de couche unique', which in French reads as 'single layer' rather than 'distinct layers'. The calque 'exercer les chemins d'options' / 'exercer l'étape' ([51], [53]) is stiff.

examples.source: Update any code that references `job.primitive_id`.
examples.translation: Met à jour tout code qui référence `job.primitive_id`.
examples.suggested: Mets à jour tout code qui référence `job.primitive_id`.
examples.why: The tu imperative of 'mettre' is 'mets'. 'Met' is a conjugation error, repeated in [20] and [22].

examples.source: any helper (such as the unique-layer helper)
examples.translation: tout assistant (tel que l'assistant de couche unique)
examples.suggested: tout utilitaire (tel que l'utilitaire d'extraction des couches distinctes)
examples.why: 'Couche unique' means 'single layer', but the source means 'distinct/deduplicated layers'. The same ambiguity appears in [26] ('les couches uniques').

examples.source: local testing only needs to exercise the option paths
examples.translation: le test local a seulement besoin d'exercer les chemins d'options
examples.suggested: le test local n'a besoin que de parcourir (tester) les chemins d'options
examples.why: 'Exercer' calques the English 'exercise'. A French engineer would write 'tester' or 'parcourir'. The same calque appears in [51].

examples.source: | Change | Migration action |
examples.translation: | Change | Migration action |
examples.suggested: | Changement | Action de migration |
examples.why: The table header was left in English, but it is translatable prose.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The compatibility claims in [10] and [35] ("fonctionne uniquement avec…"), the Estimator caveat in [38] and the underscore-vs-hyphen note in [28] are all kept intact, and I found no drift. The slips are small. [30] has a wrong imperative: "Met à jour" should be "Mets à jour". The bold labels in [18], [20] and [36] use a calqued "en travaillant avec", and [7] has the word order "l'original NoiseLearner". "Box"/"boxed" is rendered as "encadré"/"encadrées", which in French suggests a layout sidebar; "boîte"/"mises en boîte" would suit the BoxOp concept better, but readers will still recognise it.

examples.source: Update your code if it inspects the output explicitly.
examples.translation: Met à jour ton code s'il inspecte explicitement la sortie.
examples.suggested: Mets à jour ton code s'il inspecte explicitement la sortie.
examples.why: The tu-form imperative of 'mettre' needs a final -s; 'Met' is a spelling/grammar error.

examples.source: **`NoiseLearnerV3`, when working with client-side Estimator:**
examples.translation: **`NoiseLearnerV3`, en travaillant avec Estimator côté client :**
examples.suggested: **`NoiseLearnerV3` avec l'Estimator côté client :**
examples.why: 'en travaillant avec' is a word-for-word calque of 'when working with'; the same pattern appears in [20] and [36].

examples.source: Unlike the original `NoiseLearner`, ... takes a list of boxed circuit instructions
examples.translation: Contrairement à l'original `NoiseLearner`, ... une liste d'instructions de circuit encadrées
examples.suggested: Contrairement au `NoiseLearner` d'origine, ... une liste d'instructions de circuit mises en boîte
examples.why: 'l'original X' follows English word order. 'encadrées/encadré' for box/BoxOp reads like a layout sidebar; it is used the same way in [8], [17], [19] and [21].

editor_note: None of the five rewritten entries would mislead a learner. Entry 8 correctly ties NoiseLearner to EstimatorV2 côté serveur and NoiseLearnerV3 to Executor and the new Estimator côté client (v0.50.0), and entry 17 keeps "nombre maximum de couches à apprendre" and "stratégie de twirling". The one terminology slip is in entry 36, which renders "helper program" as "programme d'assistance". The rest of the page uses "assistant", as in the title "Assistant d'apprentissage du bruit" and "cet assistant" in entries 11 and 25. The heading in entry 35 also leaves out the article before Estimator, which reads stiffly in French.

examples.source: The following code shows how to use the helper program with the new client-side Estimator
examples.translation: Le code suivant montre comment utiliser le programme d'assistance avec le nouvel Estimator côté client
examples.suggested: Le code suivant montre comment utiliser cet assistant avec le nouvel Estimator côté client
examples.why: The rest of the file renders 'helper (program)' as 'assistant' (entries 1, 11, 25). 'programme d'assistance' is a different term and also sounds like a support or aid scheme.

examples.source: Using NoiseLearnerV3 with client-side Estimator
examples.translation: Utiliser NoiseLearnerV3 avec Estimator côté client
examples.suggested: Utiliser NoiseLearnerV3 avec l'Estimator côté client
examples.why: The English heading drops the article, but French needs one before a noun modified by 'côté client'. Without it the heading reads like a calque.

editor_note: The six rewritten entries (3, 13, 14, 17-19) keep the source's meaning and read naturally in the "tu" register, with terms that match the rest of the page: "flux de travail prêts à l'emploi", "modèle de fonction applicative", "gestion des entrées/sorties" and "dynamique hamiltonienne AQC + Trotter".

Both rewritten entries keep the English meaning, and nothing in them would mislead a learner. Entry 30's second sentence has two errors: "bornes de horodatage" is missing the elision ("d'horodatage"), and "sur quand des shots particuliers ont été exécutés" is copied from English syntax and isn't grammatical French. Entry 6 has one smaller slip: "options de runtime spécifiées depuis la primitive" copies "specified from" word for word, where "définies dans la primitive" is the natural French. "Informations de temporisation" in entry 30 is still recognizable, though "informations temporelles" would sound more natural.

examples.source: This timing information can be used to place upper and lower timestamp bounds on when particular shots were executed on the QPU.
examples.translation: Ces informations de temporisation peuvent être utilisées pour placer des bornes de horodatage supérieures et inférieures sur quand des shots particuliers ont été exécutés sur le QPU.
examples.suggested: Ces informations temporelles permettent d'encadrer par des horodatages inférieur et supérieur le moment où certains shots ont été exécutés sur le QPU.
examples.why: "de horodatage" is missing the elision, and "sur quand" is copied from English syntax and isn't grammatical in French. The meaning survives, but no native writer would phrase it this way.

examples.source: the runtime options specified from the primitive
examples.translation: des options de runtime spécifiées depuis la primitive
examples.suggested: des options de runtime définies dans la primitive
examples.why: "spécifiées depuis" copies the English "specified from" word for word, and French doesn't use "depuis" this way.

editor_note: The translation is faithful and reads naturally, and the addon names are rendered consistently as "Extension Qiskit de …" (for example "rétropropagation d'opérateurs (OBP)" and "diagonalisation quantique par échantillonnage (SQD)"), with the Dependabot advice carried over intact in the "tu" register.

The rewritten entry 6 keeps the English meaning. The caveat that exact simulation does not reflect real hardware results is there, the reference primitives still lack noise modelling while Aer supports it, and the Aer-instead-of-reference-primitives claim is intact. The informal "tu" register holds. One naturalness slip: "sujets à des erreurs, ou bruits" copies the English appositive but uses the plural "bruits", which reads oddly in French. Here noise is an uncountable physical phenomenon, and a native editor would write "des erreurs, autrement dit du bruit".

examples.source: Currently existing quantum processors suffer from errors, or noise,
examples.translation: Les processeurs quantiques actuels sont sujets à des erreurs, ou bruits,
examples.suggested: Les processeurs quantiques actuels sont sujets à des erreurs, autrement dit du bruit,
examples.why: The plural 'bruits' copies the English 'errors, or noise' appositive awkwardly. In French technical usage, noise in this sense is uncountable ('du bruit'). The meaning is unaffected.

editor_note: Entry 17 is faithful: the data shared (nom, adresse e-mail, badge obtenu), the Credly e-mail, the purposes, sharing with IBM subsidiaries and third parties, and the privacy-statement link all match the English, and the "tu" register holds. It has two calques a native editor would fix. "data processor" is rendered as "processeur de données", but the standard French privacy/RGPD term is "sous-traitant (de données)". "claiming the badge" is rendered as "réclamer le badge", which in French suggests a complaint or demand; "récupérer" or "accepter le badge" is the natural wording. The period also sits inside the link text ("[ici.]"), which is cosmetic only.

examples.source: Credly, a third-party data processor authorized by IBM
examples.translation: Credly, un processeur de données tiers autorisé par IBM
examples.suggested: Credly, un sous-traitant tiers de traitement des données autorisé par IBM
examples.why: In French privacy/RGPD wording, 'data processor' is 'sous-traitant'. 'Processeur de données' is a literal calque.

examples.source: with instructions for claiming the badge
examples.translation: avec les instructions pour réclamer le badge
examples.suggested: avec les instructions pour récupérer ton badge
examples.why: 'Réclamer' suggests making a complaint or demand. It is a calque of 'claim'. 'Récupérer' or 'accepter' is the idiomatic choice.

editor_note: Entry 48 matches the English: "un nombre *pair* de qubits affectés sur chaque ligne de réseau horizontale et chaque ligne de réseau verticale", the "en entrant… en ressortant" crossing explanation, and "réduites à l'identité en les multipliant par des générateurs de stabilisateurs $X$" all say what the source says, and the italic *pair* mirrors *impair* in entry 49.

None of the three rewritten entries would mislead a learner, and the informal "tu" register holds throughout. Entry 12 uses a calqued passive with a dangling infinitive: "Cet examen est destiné à être passé après avoir lu les leçons". Entry 17 contains anglicisms and calques: "exploite les services" for "leverages", "réclamer le badge" for "claim" and the bare English "reporting". Entry 10 renders "gain knowledge on" as "approfondir", which slightly assumes the reader already knows the subject.

examples.source: This exam is intended to be taken after reading the lessons in this course.
examples.translation: Cet examen est destiné à être passé après avoir lu les leçons de ce cours.
examples.suggested: Passe cet examen après avoir lu les leçons de ce cours.
examples.why: This is a calqued passive construction. Its infinitive clause has no matching subject, which reads stiffly in French.

examples.source: IBM leverages the services of Credly ... instructions for claiming the badge ... for program reporting and operational purposes
examples.translation: IBM exploite les services de Credly ... pour réclamer le badge ... à des fins de reporting et d'exploitation du programme
examples.suggested: IBM fait appel aux services de Credly ... pour récupérer ton badge ... à des fins de suivi et de gestion opérationnelle du programme
examples.why: 'Exploite' and 'réclamer' are literal renderings of 'leverages' and 'claiming', and 'reporting' is an unnecessary anglicism. A native editor would change all three.

examples.source: who are eager to gain knowledge on the theoretical foundations
examples.translation: qui ont envie d'approfondir les fondements théoriques
examples.suggested: qui souhaitent acquérir des connaissances sur les fondements théoriques
examples.why: 'Approfondir' means to deepen, which implies the reader already knows the subject. The English only says 'gain knowledge'. This is a small shift in nuance and would not mislead.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The query-model framing, the "extremely unlikely any time soon, if ever" caveat and the subroutine argument all come through intact, and "théorie algorithmique des nombres" is a good rendering of "computational number theory". Three passages read as calques from the English. In [3], "une question bien plus difficile à laquelle répondre" is followed right away by "pour y répondre", so the verb repeats. In [6], "n'est pas que ... mais plutôt parce qu'elle" mixes two constructions. Also in [6], "d'une importance critique" copies "critically important" where "capitale" or "cruciale" would sound more natural.

examples.source: This turns out to be a much more difficult question to answer, and to address it we must first establish a solid foundation
examples.translation: Il s'avère que c'est une question bien plus difficile à laquelle répondre, et pour y répondre nous devons d'abord établir une base solide
examples.suggested: Il s'avère que cette question est bien plus difficile à trancher, et pour l'aborder nous devons d'abord établir une base solide
examples.why: "difficile à laquelle répondre" copies the English sentence structure, and "répondre" appears twice in a row.

examples.source: The reason this task is important is not because we hope ... but rather because it opens up many interesting possibilities
examples.translation: La raison pour laquelle cette tâche est importante n'est pas que nous espérons ... mais plutôt parce qu'elle ouvre de nombreuses possibilités
examples.suggested: Cette tâche est importante non pas parce que nous espérons ... mais parce qu'elle ouvre de nombreuses possibilités
examples.why: The sentence mixes "n'est pas que" with "parce que", which follows the English and is ungrammatical in careful French.

examples.source: a critically important task
examples.translation: une tâche d'une importance critique
examples.suggested: une tâche d'une importance capitale
examples.why: "importance critique" copies the English wording; "capitale" or "cruciale" is the idiomatic French choice.

editor_note: Entry 9 is faithful and reads naturally: it uses the standard terms "matrices densité", "canaux" and "mesures", keeps the comparison "classe de mesures plus générale que celles présentées dans Bases de l'information quantique", and renders the operational link to channels and measurements correctly as "se rattachent, sur le plan opérationnel, aux canaux et aux mesures".

Nothing here would mislead a learner. The exam, badge and Credly privacy notice keep their full meaning and caveats, and the "tu" register holds throughout. A few phrases are calqued from English. The meta description opens with "Construit les bases", where French would say "Pose les bases". "Tu seras notifié par Credly" copies the English passive; "Credly t'informera" reads more naturally. "Réclamer ton badge" is a literal calque of "claiming"; "récupérer ton badge" is the usual phrasing.

examples.source: Builds foundations of quantum computing, technology, and business applications.
examples.translation: Construit les bases du calcul quantique, de la technologie et des applications commerciales.
examples.suggested: Pose les bases du calcul quantique, de sa technologie et de ses applications métier.
examples.why: 'Construire les bases' is a calque of 'build foundations'; French says 'poser les bases'. Using 'métier' here would also match 'problèmes métier' in [4].

examples.source: Once you have passed the exam, you will be notified by Credly that you have earned a badge.
examples.translation: Une fois que tu auras réussi l'examen, tu seras notifié par Credly que tu as obtenu un badge.
examples.suggested: Une fois l'examen réussi, Credly t'informera que tu as obtenu un badge.
examples.why: The passive 'être notifié par X que' copies the English structure and reads stiffly in French.

examples.source: with instructions for claiming the badge
examples.translation: avec les instructions pour réclamer ton badge
examples.suggested: avec les instructions pour récupérer ton badge
examples.why: 'Réclamer' suggests demanding something you are owed. 'Récupérer' is the idiomatic word for collecting a badge.

editor_note: Neither rewritten entry changes the meaning. Entry 44 (the video title) is faithful and reads naturally: "présente un bref aperçu des réseaux de neurones et de la manière dont les circuits quantiques peuvent former des structures analogues". The one problem is the heading in entry 9, "Introduire « quantique » dans l'apprentissage automatique". It has no article, so it sounds like inserting the word "quantique" rather than the concept. It also doesn't match the very next paragraph (entry 10), which says "le « quantique »". Adding "le" fixes both.

examples.source: Introducing “quantum” to machine learning
examples.translation: Introduire « quantique » dans l'apprentissage automatique
examples.suggested: Introduire le « quantique » dans l'apprentissage automatique
examples.why: Without an article, the quoted adjective sounds like the word itself is being inserted. French uses "le quantique" as a noun for the concept, which entry 10 already does ("comment le « quantique » est introduit"), so the heading should match.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The facts all match the English: 20 questions, at least 16 correct to pass, and the exam locks after two failed attempts. Entry [8] has a clumsy construction, "tu dois en répondre correctement à au moins 16", because "en" does not work with "répondre à". Entry [12] renders "claiming the badge" with the calque "réclamer ton badge", and entry [5] uses "Félicitations pour avoir terminé" where "Félicitations d'avoir terminé" would be the idiomatic form. The informal "tu" register holds throughout.

examples.source: you must answer at least 16 correctly to pass
examples.translation: tu dois en répondre correctement à au moins 16 pour réussir
examples.suggested: tu dois répondre correctement à au moins 16 d'entre elles pour réussir
examples.why: "en répondre à" is ungrammatical: "répondre" takes "à", not "en".

examples.source: instructions for claiming the badge
examples.translation: les instructions pour réclamer ton badge
examples.suggested: les instructions pour récupérer ton badge
examples.why: "Réclamer" copies the English "claim" and suggests demanding something owed. "Récupérer" is the usual French word for collecting a badge.

examples.source: Congratulations on completing this course!
examples.translation: Félicitations pour avoir terminé ce cours !
examples.suggested: Félicitations d'avoir terminé ce cours !
examples.why: "Félicitations d'avoir" is the idiomatic construction before an infinitive.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the GHZ accidental-protection argument in [137]-[152], so nothing here would mislead a learner. The terms are split, though. "Pauli twirling" stays in English up to [129] and then becomes "twirling de Pauli" from [150] onward. Measurement counts are "décomptes" early on and "comptages" in [154] and [164]. [5] slips into vous ("gardez à l'esprit"), and a few calques read stiffly: "un cas convaincant pour le Pauli twirling en détruisant…" in [121], "plus de 20 % meilleures" in [69], "soigneusement bien isolés" in [47], and the double negation in [95].

examples.source: Pauli twirling fundamentally changes this situation.
examples.translation: Le twirling de Pauli change fondamentalement cette situation.
examples.suggested: Le Pauli twirling change fondamentalement cette situation.
examples.why: The earlier half of the file consistently uses 'le Pauli twirling'. From [150] on it switches to 'twirling de Pauli', so the term is inconsistent within the file.

examples.source: but keep in mind that these methods are not limited to the examples shown here
examples.translation: mais gardez à l'esprit que ces méthodes ne se limitent pas aux exemples présentés ici
examples.suggested: mais garde à l'esprit que ces méthodes ne se limitent pas aux exemples présentés ici
examples.why: This is a formal vous slip on a page that otherwise uses tu (e.g. 'Garde à l'esprit' in [115]).

examples.source: The previous example showed a compelling case for Pauli twirling in destroying the coherent accumulation of errors
examples.translation: L'exemple précédent a montré un cas convaincant pour le Pauli twirling en détruisant l'accumulation cohérente d'erreurs
examples.suggested: L'exemple précédent a montré de façon convaincante l'intérêt du Pauli twirling pour détruire l'accumulation cohérente d'erreurs
examples.why: 'un cas convaincant pour' is calqued from English, and the gérondif 'en détruisant' grammatically attaches the destroying to the example rather than to the twirling.

examples.source: To be clear, one does not choose a single twirling pattern and use it throughout the circuit.
examples.translation: Pour être clair, on ne choisit pas un seul motif de twirling et on ne l'utilise pas tout au long du circuit.
examples.suggested: Précisons-le : on ne choisit pas un motif de twirling unique pour l'utiliser tout au long du circuit.
examples.why: The doubled negation is clumsy and slightly blurs the point, which is not to reuse one pattern everywhere.

examples.source: the expectation values with DD are typically more than 20% better (closer to 1) than the values without DD
examples.translation: les valeurs d'espérance avec DD sont généralement plus de 20 % meilleures (plus proches de 1) que les valeurs sans DD
examples.suggested: les valeurs d'espérance avec DD sont généralement supérieures de plus de 20 % (plus proches de 1) à celles obtenues sans DD
examples.why: 'plus de 20 % meilleures' is an English calque. The comparative is more natural in French when built with 'supérieures de'.

editor_note: Entry 64, "5.3 Post-process", is correctly rendered as "5.3 Post-traitement". It is the standard French term, it matches "Post-traiter" in entry 48, and the anchor is unchanged. Note that the sibling heading in entry 55 still reads "Étape 4 : Post-process", but that entry was outside this review.

Entry 82 is faithful and reads naturally: "Tu peux configurer les options de suppression des erreurs dans Sampler V2" keeps the "tu" register, and the rendered link text "Gestion du bruit du Sampler" plus "la référence de l'API ExecutionOptionsV2" add or drop nothing.

Both rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally. [20] renders the shots/accuracy/cost trade-off as "Plus il y a d'exécutions (ou *shots*), plus les résultats seront précis", and [27] keeps the "we often don't know its eigenbasis" caveat as "base propre", with "valeur d'espérance" and "dispositif quantique" used the same way as in the rest of the page.

The meaning is faithful throughout, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The 16/20 pass threshold, the two-attempt lockout and the Credly notice all match the source, and "tu" is used consistently. A native editor would still fix three small slips. In [8], "tu dois en répondre correctement au moins 16" is ungrammatical, because "répondre" takes "à", not "en". In [7], "badging exam" becomes "examen de certification", which blurs IBM's line between a badge and a certification. In [5], "Félicitations pour avoir terminé" is less idiomatic than "Félicitations d'avoir terminé".

examples.source: you must answer at least 16 correctly to pass
examples.translation: tu dois en répondre correctement au moins 16 pour réussir
examples.suggested: tu dois répondre correctement à au moins 16 d'entre elles pour réussir
examples.why: The verb is "répondre à", so the pronoun "en" is ungrammatical here. The sentence reads as a calque.

examples.source: take the badging exam for Variational algorithm design
examples.translation: passer l'examen de certification pour la conception d'algorithmes variationnels
examples.suggested: passer l'examen du badge Conception d'algorithmes variationnels
examples.why: IBM treats badges and certifications as separate credentials. "Certification" slightly overstates what this exam awards; the page itself says "Examen et badge".

examples.source: Congratulations on completing this course!
examples.translation: Félicitations pour avoir terminé ce cours !
examples.suggested: Félicitations d'avoir terminé ce cours !
examples.why: Before an infinitive, "Félicitations d'avoir" is the idiomatic construction. "Pour avoir" reads as a calque.
